title: CRLR/68/2013 of SMT. ROSHNI ALIAS  PRITI SEXANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.68 of 2013
Smt. Roshni @ Priti Sexana ...Revisionists
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Another ...Respondents
Mr. Manoj Mohan, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for respondent no.2.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit
Instant criminal revision has been preferred against the
judgment and order dated 01.12.2012 passed by learned Principal
Judge Family Court, Haridwar in Case No.20 of 2011 Smt. Roshni @
Priti Sexana vs. Sri Ramakant Sexana under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
whereby learned Judge Family Court has rejected the application
moved by revisionist no.1 and allowed the application of revisionist
no.2 and 3 as mother/natural guardian of revisionist nos.2 & 3 and
directed respondent no.2-husband to pay a sum of Rs.1,000/- each per
month to the revisionist nos.2 & 3 as maintenance from the date of
order i.e. 01.12.2012
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. The revisionist has challenged the rejection of her maintenance
as well as sought enhancement of maintenance of her children i.e
revisionist nos.2 & 3. An application for maintenance under Section
125 of Cr.P.C. was moved on behalf of the revisionists on 01.12.2012
against respondent no.2-husband with the averments that revisionist
no.1-Smt. Roshni @ Priti Sexana and respondent no.2-Ramakant
Sexana were married according to Hindu rites and rituals, in the year
2002. Out of this wedlock two daughters, namely, Km. Disha and Km.
Reet were born. It was contended by revisionist no.1-wife that after
marriage the relation between them have become sour and family
members of respondent no.2 started cruelty with her due to the reason

2
that two daughters were born; on 20.09.2007 she was turned out of the
house by her husband. She further narrated that after that day
respondent no.2 had no concern with the revisionist-wife and his
daughters and nothing was done for their survival by him.
4. So far as the income of husband is concerned, it is alleged in
the petition that respondent no.2 has income of Rs.50,000/- per month
while revisionist no.1-wife being sparsely educated was not in a
position to maintain herself and her daughters. She claimed Rs.5,000/-
per month as maintenance for herself and Rs.3,000/- per month each,
for her daughters.
5. The case was contested by respondent no.2 by filing objection
in which the marriage was admitted and it was also admitted that
revisionist no.2 and 3 were born out of the said wedlock. So far as the
aspect of the cruelty towards demand of dowry is concerned, the same
was denied and this fact as also been denied that revisionist and the
daughters were turned out by the respondent no.2. Rather it was
submitted that when respondent no.2 was out of his house in
connection with his employment, he was informed that revisionist
no.1-wife had left the house without his permission and in his
absence, his mother-in-law had taken away his wife-revisionist no.1
with minor daughters. Attempt was made by respondent no.2 to take
her wife-revisionist no.1 back to her in-laws house but she
categorically refused to join the company of respondent no.2. It is
further contended by respondent no.2 that his mother-in-law told him
that her daughter was already married with Vikas @ Guddu, son of
Abhilash Chand Sexana, who was ready to keep her daughter with
him. The mother-in-law of respondent no.2 further stated that they
want to send her daughter (wife of respondent no.2) with Vikas @
Guddu.
6. Learned trial court after going through the evidence on record
has given a very thoughtful consideration as to whether revisionist

3
no.1-wife is entitled to get maintenance from respondent no.2 owing
to the fact that she was not legally wedded wife of respondent no.2.
The learned trial court has come to the conclusion that revisionist no.1
admitted in her evidence that she was married to Vikas @ Guddu,
who was her ex-husband but at the same time it was also admitted by
her that there was a divorced outside the court at the instance of ex-father-in-law-Shri Abhilash Chand Sexana of revisionist no.1 with the
consent of respondent no.2.
7. Learned court below recorded a finding that since first marriage
of revisionist no.1 was not dissolved legally by a decree of court,
revisionist no.1 cannot be proved a legally wedded wife of respondent
no.2 and accordingly, rejected the application filed under Section 125
of Cr.P.C. moved by revisionist no.1 for maintenance and only
allowed the maintenance in respect of revisionist nos.2 & 3.
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that divorced
between ex-husband and revisionist no.1 is protected under Section 29
of the Hindu Marriage Act and, therefore, it cannot be said that
divorce was not legal and consequently marriage of revisionist no.1
with respondent no.2 was not legal.
9. I have considered the arguments submitted on behalf of the
revisionist with the provision of Section 29 of Hindu Marriage Act,
which is quoted hereunder:-
"29 Savings. (1) A marriage solemnized between Hindus before
the commencement of this Act, which is otherwise valid, shall not
be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid by reason
only of the fact that the parties thereto belonged to the same gotra
or pravara or belonged to different religions, castes or sub-divisions of the same caste.
(2) Nothing contained in this Act shall be deemed to affect any
right recognised by custom or conferred by any special enactment
to obtain the dissolution of a Hindu marriage, whether solemnized
before or after the commencement of this Act.
(3) Nothing contained in this Act shall affect any proceeding under
any law for the time being in force for declaring any marriage to be
null and void or for annulling or dissolving any marriage or for
judicial separation pending at the commencement of this Act, and
any such proceeding may be continued and determined as if this
Act had not been passed.

4
(4) Nothing contained in this Act shall be deemed to affect the
provisions contained in the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (43 of
1954) with respect to marriages between Hindus solemnized under
that Act, whether before or after the commencement of this Act."
10. It is needless to say that if a person asserts custom it has to be
shown by pleading as well as by evidence that the custom was old
one, it has been in practice even on the date and same has been given
effect to by the parties.
11. From the pleadings of the parties as well as from the evidence
adduced by the revisionist, there is no such proof about the existence
of the custom of taking divorce in such a manner and that it was
prevalent in the caste and society to which parties to the matrimony
belonged. Hence, this argument does not hold any water and the same
is liable to be rejected. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and
order dated 01.12.2012 passed by the learned Judge, Family Court,
Haridwar does not need any interference by this Court and the same is
affirmed so far as it relates to the rejection of petitioner's claim for
maintenance.
12. So far as the maintenance awarded to revisionist nos.2 and 3 is
concerned, this Court has gone through the pleadings of the parties. In
the petition under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. it has been pleaded by the
revisionist that the income of respondent no.2 was Rs.50,000/- per
month which he earned by doing business of property dealing.
13. Respondent no.2 in his objection denied that income but in para
15 of the reply/objection it has been stated that respondent no.2 earned
his living by doing labour. From the reply submitted by respondent
no.2 that after marriage respondent no.2 helped the family of his in-laws, it is clear that his condition was better than that of the family of
the in-laws; even otherwise if it is believed that revisionist earned his
living by doing labour work in the year 2011 the income of a labour
would be approximately Rs.12,000/- per month. The maintenance

5
granted by learned Judge, Family Court appears to be on a very lower
side i.e. Rs.1,000/- each per month.
14. This Court is of the view that respondent no.2 earns Rs.50,000/-
per month as alleged by revisionist no.1-wife and the denial by saying
that he works as a labour, it would be appropriate to award the sum of
Rs.3,000/- per month each to revisionist nos.2 & 3, assessing the
income of respondent no.2 @ of Rs.12,000/- per month. Learned
Judge Family Court has allowed the claim petition by awarding
maintenance at the rate of Rs.1,000/- each from the date of order, but
the maintenance after having been enhanced by this Court at the rate
of Rs.3,000/- per month each to revisionist nos.2 & 3, would be
payable from the date of filing of the application. The maintenance
awarded is to be given on or before 12th of every month and the
arrears of maintenance so awarded is to be given within a period of
two months, with adjusting the amount of compensation already paid.
15. Accordingly, the revision is partly allowed.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 22.06.2023
